The decisive fact in this profile is avg_degree = 88.28 on 11,758 nodes (density 0.015, max_degree 2138). Every neighbour-relative view is read against a neighbour average built from ~88 rows, which converges to the global mean, so local_affinity, homophily_violation, spectral (one-hop residual, and n > 3000 forces the smoothing branch rather than the eigenvector branch) and attr_struct_mismatch (which inherits the neighbour-relative half) are all in their stated degenerate regime. Their wide landmarker spreads are consistent with a degree confound, low-degree nodes deviating more from a small neighbour average, not with anomaly signal, and a landmarker cannot distinguish the two. contrastive is ruled out by its own degeneracy condition: feature_sparsity 0.48 and feature_dup_rate 0.489 on only 10 dimensions mean attribute dropout changes almost nothing, so every node looks stable. one_class carries a documented collapse failure in this implementation, with no preview to check it against. density reads no edges, which would be complementary, but its landmarker is p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0 with mass only above p99: with 48.9% byte-identical rows in 10 dimensions, the 20 nearest neighbours are frequently exact duplicates, so LOF is flat for most of the graph and would contribute mostly ties. conformity is applicable on paper (dup_rate 0.489), but at 10 dimensions with 48% zeros a high duplicate rate is close to unavoidable and is weak evidence of a deliberate template mechanism; its scores are compressed exactly where it matters (p90 0.936, p95 0.949, p99 0.969, so the top of its ranking is a near-tie), and its inverted sign means a wrong call is actively anti-correlated rather than merely uninformative. That leaves two views whose reference frames survive the degree. reconstruction is the only paradigm with a preview, and the preview is the most anomaly-shaped distribution here: tight body (p50 0.042, p90 0.080) with a genuine tail (p99 0.234, roughly 3x p90), at rank correlation 0.87 with the full run. Its high-degree caveat is that the error ends up ranking nodes by distance from the global attribute mean, which in this 10-dimensional, template-dominated attribute space is still a reasonable global outlierness signal, just not a neighbourhood one. community is supported directly by the partition statistics: modularity 0.519 is well above the ~0.3 floor, homophily 0.749 of edges stay inside a community, and 26 communities over 11,758 nodes gives roughly 450 nodes each, so the centroids are far from the global mean and the partition has something real to measure against. Its landmarker separates at the top (p90 0.544, p95 0.599, p99 0.734). The two are complementary in reference frame, global attribute deviation versus community-relative deviation normalised by each community's own spread, and that per-community normalisation is what keeps it from collapsing onto the reconstruction view despite the high homophily. I am deliberately stopping at two rather than padding the set: every remaining candidate is either in a stated degenerate regime or sign-risky, and adding one would dilute two supported views with noise.

rationale: avg_degree = 88.28 on density 0.015 is the dominant fact in this profile: every neighbour-averaged quantity converges to the global mean, so the catalog's high-degree degeneracy fires on local_affinity, homophily_violation, attr_struct_mismatch, spectral and reconstruction alike. I therefore build the composition around reference frames that are not neighbour-averaged, and keep exactly one neighbour-relative view as a check rather than three correlated copies of it. (1) community is the best-supported view here: modularity = 0.5194 with homophily = 0.7492 is a genuinely strong partition, and 26 communities over 11758 nodes gives ~450 nodes per centroid, small enough that the centroid is not just the global mean, which is the condition under which this view degenerates. Its landmarker is the healthiest on the board: mean 0.2552, std 0.1927, a smoothly graded climb from p50 0.2295 to p90 0.5439 to p99 0.7341, no mass piled at either end. (2) one_class supplies the global frame, judging each node against the bulk rather than against its own neighbourhood, which is precisely the resolution that avg_degree 88 destroys everywhere else. feature_dim = 10 is low and feature_sparsity = 0.4803 leaves real continuous content, so the SVDD distance has something to spread over; there is no preview, but the collapse failure mode is an embedding pathology, not something this profile predicts. I prefer it over adversarial because feature_sparsity 0.4803 means half the entries are exactly zero, and additive Gaussian noise makes those zeros non-zero, so the discriminator saturates on the trivial cue. (3) homophily_violation is the one neighbour-relative view I keep, and its landmarker argues it has not actually collapsed the way avg_degree 88 predicts: std 0.1881 with p50 0.3628, p90 0.6459, p99 0.8410 is a wide graded spread, not a narrow band. I choose it over local_affinity (std 0.139, p99 0.6969) because it reads raw unnormalised rows, and with only 10 attributes the magnitude information that cosine normalisation discards is likely to carry signal; the two are explicitly near-duplicates, so taking both would buy redundancy rather than a third view. Excluded and why: contrastive is directly contraindicated, feature_dup_rate = 0.489 with feature_sparsity = 0.4803 means dropping attribute entries changes almost nothing and every node reads as stable. density is visibly dead, 48.9% byte-identical rows put zero-distance points inside the k=20 LOF neighbourhood, and the landmarker confirms it with p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0 and only p99 = 0.0476 nonzero, so the bulk has no resolution at all. conformity inverts its sign, and its distribution (p50 0.8696, mass pressed against 1) says sitting near the rank-5 dominant subspace is simply the normal condition on this graph, which is its stated degenerate case and the case where it is anti-correlated rather than merely uninformative. spectral falls to n = 11758 > 3000, so it uses the one-hop smoothing residual, and at degree 88 smoothing removes nearly everything; its landmarker sits low and compressed (mean 0.1377, p50 0.1077). attr_struct_mismatch inherits the neighbour-relative failure in one half and overlaps homophily_violation in the other. reconstruction is the closest call I drop: its 20-epoch preview is tightly banded (p50 0.0418 to p95 0.0894) with a thin spike at p99 0.234, and at avg_degree 88 the catalog warns the error degrades into distance from the global attribute mean, which is what one_class already measures more directly and without the decoder. The three kept views read the graph from three genuinely different frames, community-relative, global, and neighbour-relative, which is the complementarity this profile can actually support.

rationale: The graph has a strong, usable partition: modularity 0.5194 with 26 communities over 11758 nodes (about 450 nodes each, so centroids are not the global mean), clustering_coeff 0.5329 and homophily 0.7492, meaning edges and triangles stay inside communities. That makes community-relative comparison the best-supported reference frame here, and its landmarker orders the whole population rather than a handful of nodes (p50 0.2295, p90 0.5439, p99 0.7341). local_affinity is the neighbour-relative complement. avg_degree 88.28 is the stated failure mode for neighbour-relative views, but the same high clustering and community confinement mean a node's neighbour average is a community-level average, not the global mean, and the landmarker confirms resolution survived on this graph (spread from p50 0.1982 to p99 0.6969 rather than a constant band). I take only one of the affinity pair: the catalog says local_affinity and homophily_violation differ only in cosine-on-normalised versus distance-on-raw and are rarely independent evidence, and with feature_dim 10 of mixed scale plus feature_sparsity 0.4803 the normalised cosine version is the less scale-dominated of the two. reconstruction adds the one learned, nonlinear view: its 20-epoch preview tracks the full run (rank correlation 0.87) and shows a sharply selective top tail (p95 0.0894 to p99 0.2340), which complements the two broad-spread rankings at the top of the list even though the bulk of it is compressed by the large neighbourhoods. Excluded: density, whose landmarker is degenerate on this graph (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0), exactly as expected when feature_dup_rate 0.489 puts byte-identical rows inside the 20-neighbour ball; attr_struct_mismatch, because one half lives in that same collapsed attribute-kNN space and the other half is the high-degree neighbour view, so the rank difference is largely noise; conformity, whose mass is piled against its own ceiling (p50 0.8696, p90 0.9357, p99 0.9686) so the top of the ranking turns on tiny residual differences, and whose inverted sign makes a wrong call actively anti-correlated; contrastive, which degenerates on redundant or sparse attributes and this graph is both (feature_sparsity 0.4803, feature_dup_rate 0.489), so dropout barely moves the embedding; spectral, since n = 11758 puts it on the one-hop smoothing residual, and at density 0.015017 and avg_degree 88.28 one-hop smoothing removes almost nothing, plus it sees only the attribute norm; one_class and adversarial, both global views with no preview and a documented collapse or saturation failure, which is a poor bet on only 10 attributes when three better-evidenced frames are already available.
